claims: The 1988 Seoul Olympics were held from September 17 to October 2 in South Korea.
159 nations participated in the 1988 Seoul Olympics.
8,391 athletes participated in the 1988 Seoul Olympics.
The official motto of the 1988 Seoul Olympics was "Harmony and Progress" (화합과 전진).
The mascot of the 1988 Seoul Olympics was Hodori, a tiger dressed in traditional Korean clothing.
The theme song of the 1988 Seoul Olympics was "Hand in Hand" by Koreana.
The closing ceremony of the 1988 Seoul Olympics was held on October 2, 1988.
The closing ceremony of the 1988 Seoul Olympics featured a traditional "Talchum" masked dance.
IOC president Juan Antonio Samaranch formally closed the 1988 Seoul Olympics.
Canadian sprinter Ben Johnson won the 100m gold at the 1988 Seoul Olympics in a world-record time.
Ben Johnson tested positive for steroids at the 1988 Seoul Olympics.
Ben Johnson was disqualified from the 100m at the 1988 Seoul Olympics.
The 100m gold at the 1988 Seoul Olympics was awarded to Carl Lewis.
159 nations were represented at the 1988 Seoul Olympics, making it the largest turnout in Olympic history at the time.
The 1988 Seoul Olympics were the second Summer Games in Asia.
North Korea boycotted the 1988 Seoul Olympics.
Cuba boycotted the 1988 Seoul Olympics.
Ethiopia boycotted the 1988 Seoul Olympics.
Nicaragua boycotted the 1988 Seoul Olympics.
52 nations took home medals at the 1988 Seoul Olympics.
